summary: Makoto Kitada works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral coursework at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2008–2010) and Osaka University (attested 2026).

Makoto Nagai (1881–1970) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo, Nihon University, Toyo University, and Kamakura Women's University, and president of Chuo Shoka Junior College.

Makoto Yoshimura (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1994–2000) and served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University around 2004.
Malati J. Shendge (born 1934) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale, Akira Hirakawa, and R. D. Vadekar.

Malay Porey is an Indologist and linguist who completed an M.A. at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2012–2014). He served as Assistant Professor at Durgapur Government College, Government General Degree College, Ranibandh, and Acharya Brojendra Nath Seal College.

Malcolm David Eckel (born 1946) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Oxford and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Masatoshi Nagatomi, and was Associate Professor of Religion at Boston University (1990–2024).
Malcolm Huxter is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. (Hons) from the University of New England (1985–1991) and a Master of Psychology from Charles Sturt University (1998–2002).

Malcolm Keating is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2012–2013) and served as an assistant professor at Yale-NUS College (attested 2016–2019).

Malcolm Stuart Haughton Thompson (1885–1966) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Principal of Government College, Rajahmundry (1931–1932) and held a post at SOAS University of London (~1937–1952).
Malcolm Voyce is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at the University of London. He served as a professor at Macquarie University (attested 2009).
Malhar Kulkarni is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Organising Chair (attested 2011–2014) and held a post (attested 2024–2026) at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

Mallica Kumbera Landrus is an Indologist and art historian. She serves as Keeper of Eastern Art at the Ashmolean Museum and Associate Professor of Indian Art at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).
Mamata Dash (born 1947) is an Indology scholar. She completed her studies at Ravenshaw Girls' School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami (1937–2024) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, earning a doctorate, and held faculty posts at Kyoto University (1965–2001), Kobe University, and Otani University.
Manabendu Banerjee (born 1939) is an Indologist. He served as Co-ordinator for DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~2008–2011).

Manabu Asano is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued PhD studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and became a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and held a post as Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Manasicha Akepiyapornchai is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned a master's degree from Cornell University (2014–2022) and was appointed Assistant Professor at the University of Texas at Austin in 2022.

Mandakranta Bose (born 1938) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Oxford. She served as Director at the University of British Columbia and is a Senior Fellow at the Oxford Centre for Hindu Studies.

Mandan Mishra (1929–2001) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held a post at the University of Rajasthan, served as Principal and Chief Editor at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University, and was Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
